Decreasing biodiversity in an ecosystem can increase the spread of parasites by which of the following changes?

a. more carrying capacity
b. more food
c. more moving objects
d. more parasites
d. more parasites

Decreasing biodiversity in an ecosystem can lead to more parasites by increasing the relative abundance of parasites compared to the biodiversity of the host species. Over time, this can result in more stable and resilient host-parasite populations, making them more susceptible to parasitic infections and more easily infected by parasites from other sources.
